articles.title: Ronaldinho rolls back the years at 46, playing 45 minutes in Italy's third division after 11 years away in 2-0 victory
articles.summary: At 46, football legend Ronaldinho returns to competitive play with Italian club Ravenna, making an impact in a 2-0 derby win over Forlì after an 11-year absence from the professional realm.
articles.body: For more than a decade, Ronaldinho’s playing career belonged to the past, even if his reputation as one of football’s most gifted entertainers never quite faded. When third-tier Italian club Ravenna announced his arrival in June, the prospect of seeing the Brazilian back in competitive action seemed more like an elaborate publicity exercise than a serious sporting proposition. On Sunday, at 46, he walked out in a No. 10 shirt and made it real.Ronaldinho returns after 11 years as Ravenna beat Forlì in local derbyRonaldinho started Ravenna’s Serie C derby against Forlì on November 15, playing the first 45 minutes of a 2-0 victory at the Stadio Bruno Benelli. It was his first appearance in a competitive professional match since leaving Fluminense in 2015, bringing an 11-year absence from the game to an end.The occasion was considerably larger than an ordinary third-tier fixture. Ravenna’s usual 5,000-capacity ground had been expanded with a temporary stand accommodating another 1,800 spectators, named “R10” in honour of the Brazilian. Flares and smoke bombs filled the stands as Andrea Bocelli’s Con Te Partirò played over the stadium speakers, while Ronaldinho entered to a reception befitting a player whose influence on football extended far beyond the clubs he represented.Wearing Ravenna’s No. 10, the 2005 Ballon d’Or winner showed flashes of the close control and technical quality that defined his career. He did not score, nor did he create a clear opportunity for himself, but he was involved in the move that produced the opening goal.Giulio Donati put Ravenna ahead in the 36th minute with a strike from outside the penalty area, after Ronaldinho had helped set the attacking sequence in motion. He finished his half with 28 touches and an 81 per cent passing accuracy before acknowledging the supporters and making way for Matteo Maggio at the interval. Simone Rabbi added Ravenna’s second goal after the break to complete the 2-0 win.Ronaldinho had initially been expected to play around 30 minutes, but instead completed the entire first half. His contribution was necessarily limited by the circumstances of his return, yet the occasion was never solely about what he could produce over 90 minutes. Ravenna had brought one of football’s most recognisable figures back into a professional dressing room, and the response inside the Bruno Benelli showed what that meant to the club and its supporters.Speaking to Sky Italia afterwards, Ronaldinho said: “It went by too fast, that has always been football for me. Is this my last one? I don’t know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.“It was lovely to be here, playing, having the buildup in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.”Why Ronaldinho agreed to return to Italy at 46Ravenna’s announcement in June was initially met with considerable scepticism. Ronaldinho had not played professional football since his departure from Fluminense in 2015 and formally announced his retirement in 2018, aged 37. The idea that he would resume his playing career more than a decade after his last competitive appearance, particularly with a club in Italy’s third division, was difficult for many to take seriously.The move was driven by Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani, who had bought his hometown club in June 2024. His stated ambition was to “make young people of Ravenna fall in love with football”, and signing a player he had grown up idolising offered an unusually direct way of pursuing it.Cipriani had made no secret of the fact that he wanted Ronaldinho to appear in the derby against Forlì. The Brazilian’s debut in that fixture had been the president’s dream from the beginning, and the match provided the occasion around which the club could build its return.The two men had developed a genuine friendship after being introduced by Lorenzo Tonetti, the former co-owner of Milan’s well-known Giannino restaurant, which Ronaldinho frequented during his time at AC Milan between July 2008 and January 2011. That relationship helped turn what might otherwise have remained an unlikely proposal into an agreement.Cipriani explained his admiration for the Brazilian in an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport, saying: “I don't think there’s any other player who inspires such a love for the game as Ronaldinho does.”He also described the player's response when the possibility of returning to the pitch was raised. “That’s just how things go with Ronnie,” Cipriani told Il Resto del Carlino. “If there's a chance to have fun and excite people, he's all in.”Ronaldinho agreed immediately, according to Cipriani, and the arrangement extended beyond a one-off appearance. The former Barcelona and Brazil star also became a shareholder in Ravenna, giving him a stake in the club he had joined as a player. His arrival was facilitated by Cipriani, with the president's personal connection to the Brazilian central to bringing the deal together.Ronaldinho arrived in Ravenna on Friday and trained with the squad for the first time on Saturday, before being named in the starting line-up for the derby the following day. The short preparation period did little to diminish the anticipation surrounding his appearance.From AC Milan and Barcelona to Ravenna's Serie C projectRonaldinho’s return to Italy carried an additional connection to the country where he had already enjoyed one of the most memorable periods of his career. He represented AC Milan from July 2008 until January 2011, scoring his first goal in Italian football in a derby against Inter on September 28, 2008.That match was another occasion on which the Brazilian left his mark on a local rivalry, although the circumstances of Sunday's appearance were very different. At Milan, he was an established star competing at the highest level of European football. At Ravenna, he was returning at 46 to a club whose ambitions are centred on climbing the Italian divisions.Ravenna have not played in Serie B since 2008 and have never appeared in Serie A. They entered the weekend second in their Serie C regional group, with 29 points from 13 matches, while Forlì were 15th with 15 points. Ravenna had been reported to be six points behind leaders Spezia ahead of the fixture.The result preserved Ravenna’s position near the top of the table, but the larger significance of the derby was the fulfilment of a project that had seemed improbable when it was first announced. Ronaldinho's presence brought attention to a club competing outside Italy's top two divisions, while giving supporters an opportunity to see a player whose career had helped define an era of attacking football.Whether Sunday's appearance becomes a regular feature remains uncertain. Ronaldinho has not committed to a schedule of further matches, but his comments after the game left the possibility open. His willingness to return whenever Cipriani asks suggests that the derby may not necessarily be the only time he wears Ravenna's No. 10.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'The best there is so far': Tuchel praises England's display as they end World Cup winners Spain's 43-match unbeaten run
articles.summary: In a stunning upset, England ended Spain's remarkable 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid, showcasing an extraordinary performance under manager Thomas Tuchel. This win not only highlights England's potential but also secures their top position in the Nations League group.
articles.body: Spain had gone 43 matches without defeat, a remarkable run that encompassed a European Championship and a World Cup title, before Thomas Tuchel's England brought it to an end in Madrid. Described by Tuchel as a team capable of making the seemingly impossible possible, England delivered a commanding attacking display to establish a three-goal lead before surviving a late fightback after being reduced to 10 men to claim a 3-2 victory and finish top of their Nations League group.England end Spain’s 43-match unbeaten streak in MadridEngland became the first team in 43 matches to beat Spain, ending a run that had made the reigning world champions one of the most difficult sides in international football to overcome. La Roja had not lost since 2024 and had gone more than four years without defeat on home soil before Sunday’s meeting at the Metropolitano.The unbeaten sequence included Spain’s European Championship triumph and their subsequent World Cup success, making England’s victory a significant result for Tuchel’s side. Spain had also reached last year’s Nations League final, where they lost to Portugal on penalties. That match, however, officially counted as a draw after finishing 2-2 following extra time, meaning it did not interrupt their unbeaten record.England approached the match with considerable purpose, pressing aggressively from the opening minutes and refusing to allow Spain to settle into their usual possession-based rhythm. Declan Rice later described the opening 10 minutes as probably the best England had played in any 10-minute spell, pointing to the pressure and intensity that unsettled the hosts.Harry Kane gave England the lead from the penalty spot shortly before half-time. Ezri Konsa then headed in their second early in the second half, before Ben White made it 3-0 inside the opening hour, leaving Spain facing a deficit rarely associated with a side that had spent so long avoiding defeat.The result also offered England a measure of revenge after Spain had eliminated them at Euro 2024 and beaten them 3-2 at Wembley in the Nations League. Tuchel had spoken before the match about making the seemingly impossible possible, and his players initially delivered a performance that put Spain under sustained pressure.Elliot Anderson red card gives Spain a route backEngland appeared to have the match under control at 3-0, but Elliot Anderson’s dismissal changed the contest. The midfielder was sent off for a foul on Lamine Yamal inside the penalty area, giving Spain the opportunity to reduce the deficit from the spot.Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting penalty, and Nico Williams struck shortly afterwards following a counterattack to make it 3-2. England, suddenly down to 10 men, were left with around 15 minutes to protect their lead as Spain pushed forward in search of an equaliser.James Trafford, preferred to Jordan Pickford in goal, became increasingly important during the closing stages. He produced two saves from close range as Spain attacked with the Metropolitano crowd behind them, helping England withstand the pressure and preserve a victory that had looked considerably more comfortable before Anderson’s dismissal.The final whistle prompted jubilant celebrations among the England players. They had secured a fifth consecutive Nations League victory, finished above Spain on goal difference and taken top spot in Group A3.Thomas Tuchel calls Spain victory England’s best performance under his leadershipThomas Tuchel described England’s 3-2 victory over Spain as the best performance of his almost two-year tenure, praising his players for producing such a complete display against the reigning world champions in Madrid.Asked whether it was the finest performance since taking charge, the 53-year-old said:"Given the circumstances, the pressure and the quality and where we played -- against the reigning world champions and they are unbeaten in 43 matches."Putting the performance out there in Madrid in this environment, that was a very complete performance and the best there is so far."We are fully aware of what we put out there. What a performance we put out there for 60-65 minutes to be 3-0 up and deservedly 3-0 up."Of course, the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and the characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours so that changed everything"England had controlled the contest for more than an hour before Elliot Anderson’s dismissal gave Spain an opportunity to fight back. Tuchel acknowledged how dramatically the red card and resulting penalty shifted the momentum, but maintained that his side had deserved their three-goal advantage.Declan Rice also praised England’s collective belief, revealing that the players had travelled to Madrid expecting to win rather than simply contain Spain.“We knew we were going to beat them tonight. The messaging from the manager after the Croatia game was so positive, the message from the boys, everyone pushing together, knowing that we're going to come here and not just sit back and try and hit them on the counter.“Our first 10 minutes are probably the best we've played in a 10-minute spell -- pressure, pressure, pressure -- we could have had two or three. The red card changed the course of the game because it could have been a couple more.“If we don't go down to 10 I think we see more of the ball, we start to get more space and we see our attacking players thrive. Overall, 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against that team, unbeaten in 43, is a massive thing.”The defeat ended Spain’s record run, but did not prevent them from progressing to the Nations League quarter-finals in 2027. Both teams advanced as the two leading sides in the group, with England taking first place.For Tuchel, the victory provided a strong finish to England’s 2026 campaign. The side had reached the World Cup semi-finals before losing to Argentina and subsequently claimed third place by beating France in the play-off. England now close the year with a victory over the reigning world champions, having ended one of the longest unbeaten runs in international football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sadio Mane reportedly offers 60% pay cut to stay at Al-Nassr despite stellar form, but club still want him out
articles.summary: Sadio Mane's surprising willingness to accept a 60% pay cut to remain at Al-Nassr has been rejected by the club, despite his impressive performance. As the club considers reshaping its squad, high-profile departures, including Cristiano Ronaldo, could be on the horizon.
articles.body: Sadio Mane has reportedly offered to give up more than half his salary to extend his stay at Al-Nassr, but the Saudi club are still prepared to let him leave. The decision is particularly striking given the Senegal forward’s contribution since arriving in Riyadh, although his possible departure could form part of a wider reshaping of the squad involving Cristiano Ronaldo and Joao Felix.Al-Nassr reject Mane’s offer despite his contributionAccording to Saudi journalist Falah Al-Qahtani of the newspaper Okaz, Al-Nassr have decided against renewing Mane’s contract when it expires on June 30, 2027, at the end of the current season.Writing on his personal X account, Al-Qahtani claimed the forward’s representatives made substantial concessions in an attempt to secure another year, including an offer to reduce his current salary by 60%.The club have reportedly rejected that proposal, despite Mane remaining an important contributor since joining from Bayern Munich in the summer of 2023. His current deal is understood to carry a gross fixed salary of around €40 million per year, with performance-related bonuses estimated at a further €10 million to €12 million.Mane has made 144 competitive appearances for Al-Nassr, scoring 54 goals and providing 43 assists. His contribution also helped the club end a seven-year wait for the league title last season, making the reported decision not to extend his contract a significant sporting callIf the club follow through, Mane would be free to negotiate with other teams during the winter transfer window and leave on a free transfer when his contract expires.Cristiano Ronaldo’s future also uncertain at Al-NassrMane may not be the only high-profile departure under consideration. Ronaldo’s contract also runs until June 2027, following the two-year extension he signed in June 2025, and his future beyond that date remains uncertain.Reports have suggested the Portuguese forward could consider retirement after reaching 1,000 career goals. He currently has 985, leaving him 15 short of the milestone. However, no final decision on his future has been confirmed.The possibility of losing both Mane and Ronaldo would represent a substantial change for Al-Nassr, particularly given their importance to the club’s attack and commercial profile. It would also leave the Saudi side facing decisions about how to rebuild their forward line rather than simply replacing one departing player.Joao Felix could also leave as Al-Nassr weigh their optionsJoao Felix is another player whose future is attracting attention. His contract also expires in 2027, and Al-Nassr are reportedly exploring ways to prevent the Portuguese international from leaving on a free transfer.According to Kooora, the club’s management, led by chief executive Ahmed Al-Sultan, are seeking a solution, while Felix’s agent Jorge Mendes is reportedly working on the possibility of a return to Barcelona.Al-Nassr have an option to extend Felix’s contract unilaterally for another two seasons, which would keep him at the club until the summer of 2029. Exercising that clause, however, would come with significant financial commitments. Reports suggest the club would need to pay Chelsea €20 million and increase Felix’s annual salary from €10 million to €12.5 million.The three situations leave Al-Nassr facing important decisions ahead of the next transfer windows. Mane’s reported willingness to accept a substantial pay cut has not changed the club’s position, while Ronaldo and Felix remain tied to contracts that expire in 2027. Whether the decisions reflect a broader sporting strategy or a reassessment of the squad’s financial commitments, the coming months could bring considerable change in Riyadh.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bernardo Silva vuelve a Madrid con polémica
articles.standfirst: El responsable médico de Portugal argumenta la baja del luso ante Gales y su regreso a Madrid tras trascender que estará disponible para el partido ante el Celta de este sábado
articles.summary: El responsable médico de Portugal argumenta la baja del luso ante Gales y su regreso a Madrid tras trascender que estará disponible para el partido ante el Celta de este sábado
articles.body: el responsable de los servicios médicos de la Federación Portuguesa, José Carlos Noronha, ha querido aclarar hoy la marcha de Bernardo Silva a Madrid tras anunciar ayer que el futbolista no estaba disponible para medirse mañana a Gales. El madridista sufrió unas molestias en el primer encuentro frente a Dinamarca. En Portugal la maniobra no ha gustado al trascender hoy que el futbolista no tendrá problemas para medirse al Celta este mismo sábado y salir de la concentración sin una prueba más concluyente que confirmara una lesión. "Una breve explicación: estos dolores y contracturas musculares, incluso si las ecografías y resonancias magnéticas son negativas (lo cual no se hizo), incluso en esos casos, unos días después, estas lesiones pueden convertirse en roturas completas. Regresó al Real Madrid , donde los estudios de imagen no revelaron ninguna lesión. Recuerdo que el 50% de las quejas de los pacientes son negativas en cuanto a las imágenes. Lo que está demostrado es que si los atletas con este tipo de quejas están disponibles para un partido o entrenamiento, un porcentaje muy alto desarrolla una rotura, que puede ser completa, tres o dos días después", explicó, revelando Noronha la razón por la que no se realizó una evaluación más precisa. "También recuerdo lo siguiente: la resonancia magnética, que se usa frecuentemente en el estudio de estas lesiones, a menos que la lesión no sea muy extensa, no debe realizarse en las primeras 24 a 36 horas, ya que podría dar un falso negativo. Hemos tenido casos como este, por lo tanto, dado el tipo de molestias que presentó Bernardo, el procedimiento fue el correcto. Informamos al seleccionador nacional que no estaba en condiciones de juga", insistió el doctor. El médico portugués deja claro incluso que es normal que Bernardo Silva pueda jugar ante el Celta. "Es perfectamente normal que juegue el sábado. Fue tras el partido cuando pidió hacer algunos estiramientos. En definitiva, la lesión se produjo el día 14. Es prematuro jugar mañana porque se trata de una lesión estructural. Ahora, 7 u 8 días después, sí, es normal", concluyó.

articles.title: 'Don't Give a S--t,' Curt Cignetti Blasts Criticism of Indiana's Schedule After Win vs. Riley, USC
articles.summary: Despite improving to 9-1 with Saturday's 27-13 win over USC, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti still feels like his team isn't getting the respect it deserves.
articles.body:
Despite improving to 9-1 with Saturday's 27-13 win over USC, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti still feels like his team isn't getting the respect it deserves.

Cignetti was asked about the Hoosiers' success against top opponents this year, and he gave a lengthy answer addressing the criticism of the team's schedule.

"You get tired of the narratives sometimes," Cignetti told reporters. "'Quality win' because 'Joe Smith' was playing at the time. They ain't won a game since, but it was a quality win back then. I guess bad losses don't count anymore. ... The good thing about it is, I think it feeds into our motivation and our chip, and that's why I'm not afraid to keep it alive. And you know what? I'm 65 years old, and I really don't give a s--t."

Cignetti's testy answer came after he was told that the seven Big Ten teams Indiana has faced this season entered the games with a combined 29-10 record, went 1-6 against the Hoosiers and 8-16 after facing the defending national champs.

Indiana's lone loss of the season was a 19-15 heartbreaker against Ohio State last month. Still, the Hoosiers have remained one of the toughest teams in the country, holding each of their last six opponents to under 20 points.

Cignetti and Indiana will be back in action on Saturday against Washington in the penultimate game of the regular season.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 12 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Utah spared voters in the Associated Press Top 25 poll from having to make too many tough decisions following Week 11.
articles.body:
Utah spared voters in the Associated Press Top 25 poll from having to make too many tough decisions following Week 11.

The Utes hung on to beat Arizona 40-39, with Devon Dampier hitting Creed Whittemore for a 70-yard touchdown pass for the go-ahead score inside the final minutes of the fourth.

Kentucky was the highest-ranked team to go down, losing 21-14 to Florida. That knocked the Wildcats down from 13th to 17th.

Utah effectively has one foot in the College Football Playoff by improving to 10-0.

The Utes couldn't put Arizona away as Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita threw for 356 yards and three touchdowns. Utah didn't have the edge in time of possession, either, despite Dampier and Daniel Bray combining for 297 rushing yards.

This was undoubtedly one of the games of the year, and a lot of fans at home were probably asleep as it unfolded. The start got pushed back to 10:30 p.m. ET due to complications from the FAA ground stop on Friday.

In general, Week 11 was about consolidation rather than upheaval.

Texas didn't earn a lot of style points as Arch Manning threw three interceptions. The pass that mattered most, though, was his pinpoint throw to Raleek Brown with two seconds on the clock.

A win in Baton Rouge, no matter how you earn it, is something to celebrate, and the result will embolden the CFP selection committee for listing the Longhorns ahead of some one-loss squads.

Indiana is one such team, and coach Curt Cignetti left no doubt as to his feelings regarding the CFP rankings. It remains to be seen where the Hoosiers will sit in that Top 25, but they helped themselves by dispatching of USC 27-13.

Wake Forest was one of the biggest winners.

Beating SMU would've been a solid outcome on its own. The Demon Deacons went a step further by cruising past the Mustangs by 42 points. They've now outscored their opponents 218-21 in their last four games.

Wake's resume isn't the strongest among the title contenders. It lost to the ACC's only other rep in the CFP rankings, Miami. Non-conference wins over Akron, Purdue and Merrimack don't go very far, either.

But the Demon Deacons can only beat who's in front of them, and they're doing that in emphatic fashion right now.

articles.title: College football AP Top 25 rankings: First 9 teams don't change; Wake Forest jumps into top 10; LSU falls out of poll
articles.summary: Georgia and Utah remain on top as Liberty and Memphis enter the rankings.
articles.body:
Two weeks remain in the FBS regular season, and if last weekend showed us anything, plenty of chaos can still happen.

For example, this week's AP poll was released on Monday after last week's nationwide flight ground stop delayed the Oklahoma-Ole Miss game to Sunday . The Sooners were adamant that the Rebels caused the move, and OU's 24-17 win had to have felt that much sweeter.

The top of the poll stayed the same. No. 1 Georgia continued to show why it is the top team in the country with a dominant 48-21 win over No. 22 Missouri . The Utah Utes remained undefeated with a narrow 40-39 win over No. 23 Arizona . No. 4 UCLA also remained undefeated, handling business with a close 22-14 win over Illinois .

The first change was at No. 10: Wake Forest jumped into the top 10 after being ranked No. 11 last week, swapping spots with Texas Tech.

There wasn't much movement this week, but Nos. 11, 14 and 19 all lost, causing some shifting in the latest AP poll. Liberty found its way into the Top 25 at No. 22 as the Flames are 9-1. Memphis is the third Group of Six team to make an appearance in the poll this week, at No. 24, with the Tigers improving to 8-2 while riding a three-game win streak.

LSU dropped out of the Top 25 after l osing 22-21 to Texas .

Also receiving votes: Oklahoma, LSU, Duke, UTSA, New Mexico, South Carolina, Louisiana Tech, North Dakota State, Wyoming, Air Force, Toledo, SMU, Auburn, Missouri

articles.title: Hungary v Northern Ireland: We want to play on the biggest stages - Isaac Price
articles.summary: Before Tuesday's crucial trip to Hungary in the Nations League, midfielder Isaac Price says Northern Ireland want to play on the biggest stages.
articles.body:
When Northern Ireland step out into the Puskas Arena on Tuesday night, they hope it will be a taste of what is to come.

In the 70,000-seater stadium, which hosted the Champions League final between Paris St-Germain and Arsenal in May, Northern Ireland's destiny will be in their own hands.

In 18 months' time, Michael O'Neill's young side will hope be at the Euro 2028 finals.

But for now, they face Hungary with hopes of promotion to League A in the Nations League for the first time.

A win or a draw will do the job in Budapest, and it would be the latest step for a Northern Ireland side who continue to show encouraging signs in their development.

Worst case, NI will still have a shot at a play-off for League A in March but their sole aim is to get the job done on Tuesday.

Midfielder Isaac Price, who has grown into a key player under O'Neill, says you "have got to love the expectation".

"That's what you play football for. We're playing in a stadium where 70,000 people will be watching and then there'll be loads more at home watching," he told BBC Sport NI.

"That's what you grow up and want to do. You've got to play on the biggest stages and that's what it'll be tomorrow [Tuesday] night."

O'Neill not worried by sideline absence in Hungary

'No point' in NI playing for a draw in Hungary

The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

The average age of Northern Ireland's starting team in Saturday's 1-0 win over Ukraine was just 22.9 and eight of the starting team were aged 23 or younger.

But that has not stopped them progressing, as they are unbeaten in League B2 and have yet to concede a goal in five matches.

Price says there is "real belief within us", and he added that the team is "young and fearless".

"We want to go and make a memory for ourselves, if we can top the group and put ourselves into League A then that would be a massive achievement for us.

"If we can keep a clean sheet as well it would be massive. I think it gives us that extra belief that we're good enough to be there."

With 11 goals in 39 caps - the past 25 of which have been starts - Price has played a key role in the development of the team.

Born in England, he could have opted to play for the Three Lions or Germany but his international allegiance has long been with Northern Ireland.

Price qualifies for Northern Ireland through his grandmother, and says it has been "the best decision I've made for my career".

He came through the academy at Everton but made the switch to join Standard Liege in Belgium in 2023 - the same year he made his senior debut for Northern Ireland.

Price then joined West Bromwich Albion in the Championship in 2025, and believes being exposed to international football at a young age has helped his development at club level.

"A lot of it's down to Michael for picking me when I was 18, and he gave me the opportunity really," he said.

"Choosing to play here, I wouldn't change anything. I love every minute that I get to play and I love coming away with the lads, and it's definitely the best decision I've made."

articles.title: Braulio pregunta en media Europa por un delantero titular para el Valencia
articles.standfirst: El director deportivo sondea a decenas de equipo sobre goleadores que no están jugando y puedan salir cedidos
articles.summary: El director deportivo sondea a decenas de equipo sobre goleadores que no están jugando y puedan salir cedidos
articles.body: El Valencia necesita refuerzos desesperadamente. El equipo, que arrastra una confección ruinosa de este verano con Gourlay y Corberán al mando, está hecho al revés. Puestos triplicados y jugadores que han llegado para marcharse casi sin debutar. En ese escenario, el mercado de invierno es trascendental. O Braulio hace magia o la cosa se puede poner fea para mantener la categoría una temporada más. El reto es mayúsculo y desde que aterrizó en el club, el gallego ha llamado a decenas de equipos europeos en busca de un delantero titular. En Italia, en Inglaterra, en Francia, en Alemania y en Portugal han recibido el S.O.S de un Valencia que busca un goleador a la carrera. Con Hugo duro estancado y pitado por Mestalla, un Sadiq siendo Sadiq y un Danjuma que sigue en sus números de cero goles en más de un año, la necesidad de un delantero titular es acuciante. Las opciones, muchas de ellas, se van descartando por sí solas: sueldo, situación física, rechazo a venir al Valencia y demás situaciones que hacen que la búsqueda no sea un camino de rosas. El director deportivo, con llegada en muchos equipos europeos, ha sondeado jugadores que fueron primer nivel como el ucraniano Dovbyk, pero la lista es mucho más extensa. Hay jugadores de Premier con opciones, pero ninguna decisión tomada, más que nada porque por el momento, el club no sabe si el dinero de los americanos se va a poder utilizar. El CSD tiene hasta el seis de febrero para tomar una decisión con respecto a la operación del fondo de inversión con los Lim. Mientras no esté aprobado el intercambio de acciones, el dinero no estará disponible. Al margen de un delantero el Valencia busca un central y un jugador de banda. Para ello habrá que dar salidas, pero van a costar dinero, ya que hay jugadores como Canós o Foulquier que acaban contrato y con los que se tendrá que pactar una rescisión para hacer hueco en la plantilla.

articles.title: Indiana coach Curt Cignetti balks at weak schedule criticisms: 'I'm 65 years old and I really don't give a s***'
articles.summary: "That's all I've heard around here for three years," Cignetti said. "People like to discredit us and what we've accomplished."
articles.body:
Defending national champion Indiana remained at No. 6 in this week's AP Top 25 after defeating No. 18 USC 27-13 . The Hoosiers (9-1, 6-1 Big Ten) have held that same spot for the past five weeks in the AP poll.

Whether or not Indiana will move up from its No. 9 spot in the College Football Playoff rankings this week will be revealed on Tuesday. However, with the eight teams ahead of the Hoosiers each winning in Week 11, that ranking could hold.

During his Monday press conference, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti was asked by student reporter Ian Plaskoff about his team's 6-1 record in the Big Ten . Additionally, how those opponents have gone 8-16 after facing the Hoosiers, indicating that their physical style of play tends to leave a lasting impression.

Yet the perception that Indiana benefits from a weak schedule has lingered through the past three seasons, during which the Hoosiers have gone 36-3. Taking an opportunity to respond to that criticism, Cignetti spoke for three minutes to defend his team's accomplishments.

"Well, you know, we don't play anybody. We have a soft schedule, right?" Cignetti said. "That's all I've heard around here for three years. People like to discredit us and what we've accomplished."

The coach then highlighted wins over Northwestern and Nebraska, both of whom were undefeated before facing the Hoosiers. Indiana lost to Ohio State, but quarterback Julian Sayin was hurt in that game and the Buckeyes were defeated in their next two games.

The Hoosiers "missed a layup" by losing, according to Cignetti. But now, voters and observers are saying Ohio State's three defeats mean that Indiana didn't beat a quality opponent, despite the Buckeyes being a popular national champion pick before the season.

However, Indiana responded by winning at Michigan (4-2 at the time), then defeating Minnesota (who beat three top-25 teams before their Week 9 matchup) and USC (ranked No. 18 at 7-2).

"You get tired of the narrative sometimes," Cignetti said, before repeating his gripe that " bad losses don't count anymore ."

Despite his frustrations, Cignetti acknowleged that Indiana can still answer any questions about their achievements on the field, through their remaining two regular-season games and then the College Football Playoff.

"Look, it's all going to play out on the field," he said, acknowledging the "entertainment" value of his remarks that will probably cause some uproar in the media.

"The good thing about it is, I think it feeds into our motivation and our chip," Cignetti added before closing out his remarks. "And that's why I'm not afraid to keep it alive. And you know what? I'm 65 years old and I really don't give a s***."

Indiana travels to Seattle on Saturday to face Washington (6-4, 3-4 Big Ten) at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal boss Jorge Jesus responds to criticism from Ronaldo's mother
articles.summary: Jorge Jesus responds to claims by Cristiano Ronaldo's mother, Dolores Aveiro, that her son had been "deceived" by the Portugal manager.
articles.body:
Jorge Jesus has responded to claims by Cristiano Ronaldo's mother, Dolores Aveiro, that her son had been "deceived" by the Portugal manager.

Ronaldo, 41, retired from international football on 5 November, ending a career with his country during which he won 234 caps and scored 146 goals.

But his retirement also came less than a month after he had been given a 30-day suspension and fined £215 for walking out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark.

Portugal played their first game since Ronaldo's announcement against the Danes on Saturday, losing 4-1 at home .

While attending a Sporting event on Monday, Aveiro was asked about Ronaldo's national team retirement, and said: , external "Of course he was sad.

"They deceived him. And I'm sad, too. The defeat [against Denmark] was well-deserved. I was actually glad."

Before Portugal's Nations League game against Wales in Cardiff on Tuesday (19:45 GMT), Jesus was asked for his thoughts on Aveiro's comments.

"Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother?" he said.

"She is a lady I greatly respect - she suffered a lot to raise her children."

Asked if the debate about Ronaldo's international retirement would end, Jesus added: "I don't know when it's going to stop.

"If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer."

articles.title: Un autogol celtiña desnivela un partido sin tregua y el Alba confirma su recuperación
articles.standfirst: Los de Etxeberria se apuntan la cuarta victoria consecutiva y meten a los gallegos, que se toparon con un acertadísimo Mariño, en la lucha por la permanencia
articles.summary: Los de Etxeberria se apuntan la cuarta victoria consecutiva y meten a los gallegos, que se toparon con un acertadísimo Mariño, en la lucha por la permanencia
articles.body: Bonito espectáculo el que brindaron Albacete y Celta Fortuna en el Carlos Belmonte en un partido intenso y casi sin tregua. Idas y venidas y muchas ocasiones pero un marcador corto, mucha culpa tuvieron Mariño y Coke Carrillo, que significó una nueva victoria, la cuarta consecutiva, de un Alba que no se rinde y que aunque seguirá en descenso, empata a puntos con los dos filiales, el celtiña y el Sanse. Con Valverde como estilete, los manchegos golpearon primero y perdonaron después, incluido un penalti marrado por Soberón antes del descanso. El equipo de Fredi Álvarez, que llegaba con muchas bajas pero hizo méritos para puntuar, encadena cinco jornadas sin ganar y cinco derrotas consecutivas a domicilio y se mete de lleno en la pelea por la permanencia. El primer acto empezó igualado y apenas había asomado el Celta por medio de Ángel Arcos cuando una contra conducida por Víctor Valverde acababa en Róber González, que por la izquierda ponía un centro envenenado que Anxo desviaba a su propia portería. El gol obligaba al filial a dar un paso al frente, más dueño del balón y amenazante a balón parado, pero ahí aparecía Mariño, primero ante un remate de testa de Bajcetic y después cuando Álvaro Marín dejaba atrás a Lluís López y el guardameta lograba conjurar la ocasión más clara de los visitantes. Replegado y al contragolpe, el Alba encontraba una autopista por la izquierda: Valverde sentaba dos veces a Milla para probar a Coke, mientras Róber rozaba el palo desde lejos y Álex Rubio se topaba con el portero celeste en boca de gol. El segundo lo tuvo en bandeja antes del descanso, con un penalti por mano de Raúl, pero Soberón lo estrelló en el palo derecho. El descanso llegaba a un partido muy entretenido en el que los locales acabaron perdonando. El guion cambió tras el descanso. Aunque Róber avisaba nada más volver y Soberón también se topaba con un acertado Coke bajo palos, el Celta Fortuna adelantaba líneas y encontraba a Vald, que primero estrellaba un balón en el palo y poco después obligaba a Mariño a otra parada de mérito. Etxeberria agitaba el banquillo con Albarracín y Agus Medina, pero el filial seguía creando peligro y así Álvaro Marín se plantaba solo ante Mariño, que volvía a ganarle el duelo en la ocasión más clara de la segunda mitad. El Alba ya solo respiraba a la contra, con un disparo de Albarracín que atajaba Coke y un centro-chut de Vallejo, tras un gran recorte, que se marchaba rozando el palo... mientras Sergio Ortuño estuvo a punto de marcar un gol olímpico, pero estrelló un saque de esquina en el larguero. Hasta el final buscaron unos la sentencia y otros la igualada, pero el marcador ya no se movió y el Alba acababa amarrando la cuarta victoria seguida... no sin sufrimiento.

articles.title: Arch Manning Will Participate in Texas Senior Day Ceremony Amid 2027 NFL Draft Buzz
articles.summary: Arch Manning still has one season of college eligibility should he choose to use it, but the Texas quarterback had a straightforward reason while explaining why he plans to participate in Saturday's senior day activities against Arkansas.
articles.body:
Arch Manning still has one season of college eligibility should he choose to use it, but the Texas quarterback had a straightforward reason while explaining why he plans to participate in Saturday's senior day activities against Arkansas.

"I'm a senior, so I'm doing it," he said Monday, per Jim Vertuno of the Associated Press.

Saturday is the Longhorns' final regular-season home game, although they could still host a College Football Playoff game depending on how the 12-team field unfolds.

Manning will surely receive a welcome reception from the Texas fans when his name is announced during those senior day activities, especially after his touchdown pass in the final seconds of the last game against LSU extended the team's winning streak to four.

It was another dramatic and late victory in a season full of them for Manning, who has made critical fourth-quarter plays in close wins against Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU. Those plays are a major reason the Longhorns likely control their own destiny in the CFP race.

Yet he has also been inconsistent at times with 10 interceptions on the season, three of which happened against LSU. Perhaps another season at Texas will help him work on that consistency, although it also wouldn't be surprising if NFL teams see his potential and use an early pick on him if he does enter the draft.

B/R's NFL Scouting Department projected the nephew of Peyton and Eli Manning as the No. 4 overall pick in its most recent mock draft with the New York Jets as his landing spot.

Manning will surely have plenty to consider at the end of the season, which may or may not be his final one at the collegiate level. But if he does decide to enter the NFL draft, at least he will know he got to take part in Texas' senior day activities before leaving.

articles.title: Klopp y Alemania exprimen a la 'Oranje' de Xavi
articles.standfirst: La 'Mannschaft' cierra la Nations como primera de grupo; Paises Bajos, segunda
articles.summary: La 'Mannschaft' cierra la Nations como primera de grupo; Paises Bajos, segunda
articles.body: Y Jürgen Klopp recuperó el 'rock and roll' en Alemania. La selección germana vivió su victoria más abultada desde el 6-0 a Eslovaquia en 2025 y endosó una 'manita' (5-0) a la Países Bajos de Xavi Hernández que le permitió alcanzar el primer puesto del grupo en la última jornada de esta Nations League. Países Bajos, que recibió un severo correctivo, se 'salvó' de la eliminación gracias al 7-0 sobre Grecia de hace unos días... con la diferencia de goles general evitando el descalabro. El majestuoso Olympiastadion de Berlín era el escenario ideal para una noche que iba a entrar en los libros de historia. Primero, por ser el encuentro número 50 entre dos países que protagonizan una de las grandes rivalidades futbolísticas del Viejo Continente. Segundo, por ser el último partido de Alemania con Adidas tras 72 años de relación. La 'Mannschaft', que se 'pasará' a Nike en 2027, vestía de negro y dorado para decir adiós a la marca que los ha acompañado en sus tiempos más gloriosos. Y el homenaje sobre el verde, durante 90 minutos de juego, no pudo ser mejor. A Klopp le ha costado (derrota ante Grecia en casa y empate en el país heleno, por ejemplo), pero poco a poco 'su' Alemania empieza a carburar. Dominó en el primer tiempo y martilleó en un segundo donde el 'gegenpressing' que Jürgen convirtió en religión en Anfield retornó transformando la selección germana. Desde el 40' del primer tiempo, Alemania fue un rodillo ante una Países Bajos borrada del verde. Los de Xavi pasaron del 7-0 a Grecia (el pasado viernes) a llevarse una 'manita' este lunes en Berlín. El primero lo hizo Scherhant, antes del descanso, con un gol ya 'marca de la casa': un disparo desde el balcón del área que encontró la escuadra de Verbruggen. Y a partir de ahí, todos los demás. Gruda completó su 'show' (en la última década, solamente Musiala ha jugado un partido con Alemania completando más regates que Gruda) con el 5-0 pero, antes, Wirtz (por partida doble) y Schlotterbeck (de cabeza) también anotaban. Gruda, mientras, cedido por el Brighton en el Leipzig, firmaba doblete de pases de gol. Alemania cierra un fin de 2026 revitalizador que lo manda directamente al sorteo de cuartos de final como cabeza de serie. Con ellos, Francia, Inglaterra... y presumiblemente, Portugal. De esta lista saldrá la próxima semana el que será el rival de España en el parón de marzo. Paises Bajos, mientras, avanza como segundo y aunque el 'proceso' de Xavi Hernández es generalmente positivo... hoy a la 'Oranje' le tocó aprender.

articles.title: 'Nightmare,' Lane Kiffin Admits Losing Sleep Over LSU's Loss to Arch Manning, Texas
articles.summary: LSU fans who are having trouble sleeping after the team's fourth loss of the season aren't the only ones.
articles.body:
LSU fans who are having trouble sleeping after the team's fourth loss of the season aren't the only ones.

"I think it's a nightmare when I wake up that we didn't cover somebody to lose the game and that we lost to Texas," Kiffin said Monday when discussing Arch Manning's touchdown pass to Raleek Brown in the final seconds of the Longhorns' Saturday win over the Tigers, per Matt Baker of The Athletic.

"And then I wake up, and it's real. And then I go back to sleep for an hour, and I wake up, and it's real again."

Brown found himself wide open in the flat after motioning before the snap, and Manning found him to give Texas a 22-21 victory and all but eliminate the Tigers from the College Football Playoff.

LSU still had a timeout, which is another thing that Kiffin has constantly thought about in the ensuing days.

"That's part of the nightmare," he said. "In it, I keep seeing myself call timeout. And so, it's a lot."

There probably won't be that many college football fans who feel too badly for Kiffin and LSU after the head coach generated no shortage of headlines leaving Ole Miss near the end of last season before the Rebels played in the College Football Playoff.

He also hit the transfer portal hard and seemed to have a Tigers team that was good enough to compete for a CFP spot.

Instead, LSU is an ugly 3-4 in SEC play and could be looking at a fifth overall loss if it doesn't figure out a way to beat No. 8 Tennessee on the road in its next game.

While losses to Ole Miss, Kentucky and Texas all came down to the final minutes and could have gone the other way, LSU is not a program built on moral victories. Kiffin surely knows that and is having trouble accepting the latest in that line of defeats.

articles.title: Grecia se queda a las puertas de su Olimpo
articles.standfirst: Alemania y Paises Bajos avanzan a cuartos de final en este grupo
articles.summary: Alemania y Paises Bajos avanzan a cuartos de final en este grupo
articles.body: La selección griega no pudo lograr el billete para los cuartos de final de la Liga de Naciones pese imponerse este lunes por 1-0 a Serbia, que se despide del torneo con cero puntos en su casillero. Ni el 5-0 de Alemania a los Paises Bajos sirvió a los helenos pues o perdía Alemania... o la goleada era de época. Obligado a ganar tras complicarse, y de qué manera, la posibilidad de acceder a los cuartos de final, tras caer el pasado viernes por un contundente 7-0 en su visita a los Países Bajos, el seleccionador griego, el serbio Ivan Jovanovic, no dudó en recurrir (esta vez sí) de inicio al delantero Tasos Douvikas, suplente ante los neerlandeses. Lo cierto es que poco o nada aportó el delantero del Como italiano en una primera mitad en la que Douvikas, que apenas participó en el juego, no logró contabilizar ni un solo remate en los primeros cuarenta y cinco minutos. Todo lo contrario que Christos Tzolis, jugador del Arsenal inglés, que acaparó todo el protagonismo en el ataque griego con sus continuas incursiones por la banda izquierda, donde se convirtió en un problema irresoluble para el lateral Kosta Nedeljkovic. Más plano se mostró el equipo griego en la segunda parte en la que los jugadores locales, según iban conociendo los goles de Alemania sobre Países Bajos en Berlín, asumieron con resignación la imposibilidad de alcanzar los cuartos de final. Sin embargo, Grecia no quería despedirse de la Liga de Naciones con un empate que sabía a derrota y continuó, más a base de empuje que de buen juego, llegando cíclicamente al área rival. Una fe que encontró su premio con el gol de Giorgos Masouras, que había sustituido apenas unos minutos a un desaparecido Tasos Douvikas y que estableció en el 69 del definitivo 1-0 al enviar a la redes un centro del jugador del Benfica portugués Vangelis Pavlidis.

articles.standfirst: El lateral del Real Madrid fue el capitán de la 'Oranje' ante Alemania
articles.summary: El lateral del Real Madrid fue el capitán de la 'Oranje' ante Alemania
articles.body: Como capitán sobre el verde, Denzel Dumfries fue el primero en dar la cara después de la aparatosa derrota de Paises Bajos en Berlín. Un 5-0 dolorosísimo que, sin embargo, no evita que la selección de Xavi Hernández juegue los cuartos de final de esta UEFA Nations League. "Ha sido una mala actuación nuestra esta noche. Son goles que regalamos con demasiada facilidad, los espacios eran demasiado grandes. Esto no debería ocurrir", dijo Dumfries en 'NOS' al acabar el partido. "Perdimos muchos segundos balones, éramos débiles en los duelos y podían golpearnos fácilmente en la transición. Fue simplemente un fracaso colectivo", ampliaba. El lateral del Real Madrid quiso sacar conclusiones de lo ocurrido: "Había mucha frustración entre nosotros. Simplemente no fue una buena noche. Después de Grecia (victoria 7-0, el viernes), esto es muy amargo porque quieres seguir con esa línea y no lo hicimos esta noche". Dumfries, además, hizo autocrítica en el 1-0, el gol de Scherhant... que ocurrió ante él: "En el primer gol... retrocedo demasiado, dando demasiado espacio. Es diestro, lo sé, eso no debería pasar".

articles.standfirst: El exjugador Rafael Van der Vaart carga con dureza contra los jugadores de la 'oranje'
articles.summary: El exjugador Rafael Van der Vaart carga con dureza contra los jugadores de la 'oranje'
articles.body: La primera derrota de la era Xavi Hernández en Países Bajos ha sentado muy mal entre los neerlandeses. La dura goleada sufrida en Berlín ha desatado una ola de críticas que apuntan tanto al técnico como a los jugadores. Rafael Van der Vaart, ex internacional neerlandés, habitualmente polémico en sus declaraciones, no se mordió la lengua tras el 5-0 que les endosó Alemania: "A veces el rival te empuja hacia atrás, pero fíjense en cómo caminan. Es como si se hubieran cagado en los pantalones y llevasen un saco de patatas a cuestas. Se veían cansados y sin chispa". El que fuese finalista con Países Bajos en el Mundial de Sudáfrica en 2010, apuntó además con nombre y apellidos. Entre los señalados, el jugador del Real Madrid Denzel Dumfries: "Dumfries permitía que todos dispararan con demasiada facilidad", apuntó Van der Vaart. El propio lateral también hizo autocrítica al finalizar el partido y se señaló a sí mismo en el primer gol del partido: "En el primer gol... retrocedo demasiado, dando demasiado espacio. Es diestro, lo sé, eso no debería pasar", dijo el defensa neerlandés al finalizar el encuentro. Van der Vaart siguió señalando culpables, aunque dejó claro que el problema fue, fundamentalmente, colectivo: "Cuando ves a Veerman fallando un balón tras otro y a Reijnders con sus múltiples errores... Se podría nombrar a cualquiera, pero la verdad es que fue un desastre total", sentenció.

articles.title: Who is Leihani Zoric? Meet the 14-year-old surfing sensation who defeated Olympic champions to make history
articles.summary: At an age when most teenagers are still discovering their sporting ambitions, Leihani Zoric had already achieved something that even experienced surfers
articles.body: At an age when most teenagers are still discovering their sporting ambitions, Leihani Zoric had already achieved something that even experienced surfers could only dream of. The 14-year-old Australian stunned the surfing world by defeating Olympic and world champions to win the women's individual title at the 2026 ISA World Surfing Games in Peru. Her remarkable performance did more than earn her a gold medal. It placed her among the youngest champions in the competition's history and helped Australia secure an additional women's surfing qualification place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Leihani Zoric defeated surfing legends to claim historic goldZoric's victory on November 15 in Punta Rocas, Peru, carried extra significance because of the competitors she had overcome. She finished ahead of experienced surfers, including French Olympic bronze medallist Johanne Defay, who scored 14.67 in the final. Zoric produced a two-wave total of 15.50 to secure the title.However, her journey to the final was far from straightforward. She suffered a setback in the third round and had to fight through the repechage rounds to keep her championship hopes alive.Her toughest tests included heats against five-time world champion and Olympic gold medallist Carissa Moore and two-time world champion Tyler Wright. Zoric managed to advance from both challenging encounters, showing impressive composure against athletes she had once watched as a young fan.The teenager also had to compete in four heats on the final day. Despite the demanding schedule, she maintained her focus and delivered when the gold medal was within reach.Her triumph also helped Australia win the women's team title alongside established stars, including Wright and Stephanie Gilmore.Leihani Zoric's childhood dream received praise from Carissa MooreZoric's breakthrough was the result of years of hard work rather than a sudden rise. She had already established herself in junior surfing, winning Under-14 titles at the Occy Grom competition and the Skullcandy Oz Grom Open in 2024. She continued that success in 2025, winning the Under-14 division at the Soundboks Oz Grom Open for a third consecutive year.She also won the Under-18 title at the ISA Junior World Championships in September 2026 after receiving a wildcard entry, despite missing qualification for the Under-16 division.Her latest achievement earned praise from her childhood idol, Moore, who had watched her development closely.“I’ve been a fan of her surfing and of seeing her grow, not only in the water but out of the water. She’s an amazing human being, and the surfing world is really lucky to have her leading the way,” Moore said.Australian coach Chelsea Hedges also recognised her unusual talent, describing her as one of the most exciting athletes she had worked with.Zoric had entered the Peru competition with three goals: winning individual gold, helping Australia claim team gold and securing an additional women's Olympic quota place.She achieved all three.Sharing her happiness on Instagram, she wrote, “I came to Peru with one big dream and three goals: the individual gold, the team gold medal, and to help secure an extra women’s surfing spot for Australia at the LA28 Olympic Games.”Her achievement did not automatically guarantee her a place at the 2028 Olympics. She will still need to earn selection. But at just 14, Zoric had already given the surfing world a compelling reason to watch her next move.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino Offers Pep Guardiola Advice on USMNT Job Amid Rumors, 'It's the Perfect Moment'
articles.summary: Departing USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino, amidst rumors that the U.S. Soccer Federation is hoping to replace him with Pep Guardiola, told reporters on Monday that he would recommend the job to the former Manchester City man.
articles.body:
Departing USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino, amidst rumors that the U.S. Soccer Federation is hoping to replace him with Pep Guardiola, told reporters on Monday that he would recommend the job to the former Manchester City man.

"It's the perfect moment to arrive to the [U.S. Soccer] Federation," he said. "Everything is in the right direction. I think, of course, take [it]. Take it because he's going to find really good people, good players. The player can fit for his style; the National Training Center that wasn't [there] before."

Pochettino, 54, will be leaving the USMNT for Manchester United following Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal second leg against Haiti. But despite his departure, he believes the job he's leaving behind has become a prestigious one on the global stage.

"Now the vision from Europe, I promise, is completely different after the World Cup. Being head coach in USA now is prestigious," he told reporters. "It's Manchester United, the caliber of [Real] Madrid, Barcelona. Manchester United is coming for the coach of the USA. If you start to think that if you are another coach, maybe you are not working—[Antonio] Conte, or I don't know—you say, 'Oh, it's a great opportunity because it's not only the value of to be coach here. If Pochettino from Chelsea come here, [then goes to] Manchester United.' The vision is completely different."

Whether that's enough to attract the likes of Guardiola remains to be seen, though Jason Burt of the Telegraph reported that Pep will turn down any USMNT offers as he seeks to take a year away from the game. He added that "it has been suggested that Guardiola is open to meeting the US, but sources are adamant that he wants a year away from football and is not open to any offers."

So Guardiola probably won't be Poch's replacement, even if the latter spoke highly of the job on Monday.

articles.title: ESPN's Stephen A. Smith Asks Curt Cignetti to “Stick to Your Own Job” After He Tries to Save Rival HC From Firing
articles.summary: College football coaches usually stick together when the pressure heats up, even when they are coaching on opposite sidelines. Shortly after his No.
articles.body:
College football coaches usually stick together when the pressure heats up, even when they are coaching on opposite sidelines. Shortly after his No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers handed No. 18 USC a painful 27-13 loss in Bloomington, reigning national champion Curt Cignetti hopped on social media to defend Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley.

With USC dropping to 7-3 overall (4-3 in the Big Ten) and seeing its College Football Playoff hopes virtually vanish, fans and media, including the Los Angeles Times, began calling for Riley's job!

Cignetti wasn't having it, firing off a short post on X that quickly went viral with over 1.6 million views: "Lincoln Riley critics CLUELESS. Blind squirrel can see what he is building."

However, ESPN's Stephen A. Smith pushed back hard against that logic during a heated debate on First Take. While Smith made it clear that he deeply admires what Cignetti has accomplished at Indiana, where the Hoosiers are sitting at 9-1 and chasing back-to-back national titles, he felt the championship coach crossed a line by trying to shield a struggling rival from criticism!

"Not only do I not agree with him, I don't give a damn what he says, and he's the reigning, defending national champion. I have profound respect for Curt Cignetti, and you know why I have profound respect for Curt Cignetti? Because he gets the job done. But respectfully, stick to your own job about getting the job done, and stop trying to come to the protection of someone who doesn't deserve it," Smith said .

Smith also made sure to clarify where he stands on Riley's future in Southern California, looking straight into the camera to tell co-host Shae Cornette and analyst Paul Finebaum that he isn't actively campaigning for anyone to lose their livelihood. "I am not going to sit up here and call for the firing of Lincoln Riley," Smith explained. "But if USC decides to go in a different direction, I don't blame them."

For Smith, the biggest issue isn't just Cignetti's tweet; it is the glaring double standard across college athletics!

He pointed out that coaches bench, cut, or push out college players every single day if they fail to perform, yet when a head coach falls short year after year, other coaches suddenly demand endless "patience" and free passes!

When you look at the numbers, it is easy to see why Smith believes USC's patience should be running thin. Riley is currently the sixth-highest-paid coach in college football, earning $11.5 million a year before bonuses on a 10-year, $110 million contract, and firing him right now would trigger an estimated $70 million buyout.

Before coming to Los Angeles, Riley was a juggernaut at Oklahoma, winning 85% of his games (including a 37-7 Big 12 record), capturing four conference titles, and making three College Football Playoff appearances.

Since arriving at USC, however, his overall record sits at 42-21, and after going 11-3 in his debut season with Heisman winner Caleb Williams, he is just 31-18 over his last four seasons, tied for No. 36 in the FBS.

Even worse for USC boosters, Riley's year-by-year win totals have failed to hit double digits since that first season, going from 11-3 to 8-5, then 7-6, 9-4 (ending with an Alamo Bowl loss), and now sitting at 7-3 with just two games left.

Since USC joined the Big Ten, Riley has held a mediocre 15-10 conference record and has still never reached the College Football Playoff, even after the format expanded to 12 teams.

Even though USC landed the nation's No. 1 recruiting class and pulled off a 30-18 upset over Ohio State earlier this season, fans are still frustrated by ugly setbacks like a 24-7 road loss to unranked Wisconsin and their red-zone meltdown against Indiana, where USC scored just one touchdown in five red-zone trips and threw three interceptions.

Adding insult to injury, Smith noted that the excitement around USC football has noticeably faded, pointing out the abundance of empty seats at the historic LA Coliseum even during marquee matchups like the Ohio State game.

Meanwhile, crosstown rival UCLA has completely stolen the Southern California spotlight under first-year head coach Bob Chesney, marching to an undefeated 10-0 record (7-0 in the Big Ten) and sitting right in the middle of the playoff hunt.

With USC wrapping up its regular season against Maryland before a massive showdown with UCLA, Smith warned that if Riley loses to the Bruins and finishes with a fourth loss, keeping his job will be nearly impossible to defend.

At the end of the day, college football is a ruthless, results-driven business, especially at a blue-blood program like USC that handed Riley every resource imaginable to win championships. Whether Cignetti was being genuinely supportive or playing mind games with a conference rival, Stephen A. Smith is also within his rights to tell Cignetti to stick to his job !

articles.title: 49ers Could Add Former 2nd-Round DE After Poor Pass-Rush Performance vs Cowboys
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers have no problem moving the ball and putting up points. Getting to the quarterback, however, is another story.Brock Purdy and the 49er...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have no problem moving the ball and putting up points. Getting to the quarterback, however, is another story.

Brock Purdy and the 49ers put up 46 points in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium to improve to 8-1. But the defense struggled to bring down Dak Prescott, who completed 30 of 51 passes for 343 yards, five touchdowns, and an interception.

Prescott was sacked once, but that came on a play when he ran out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage. San Francisco's defensive line puts pressure on the QB. But the problem is that pressure hasn't turned into sacks.

That's why one Bay Area voice thinks a potential fix could be sitting on a practice squad in Las Vegas.

Azeez Ojulari Named Pass-Rush Target for 49ers

Former NFL scout and "Krueg Show Pod" host Larry Krueger believes San Francisco needs more speed off the edge, which is why he named four practice-squad edge-rushers the 49ers should pursue, including former Giants second-round pick Azeez Ojulari.

"The #49ers clearly lack explosive edge rush," Krueger wrote . "The DE group of Nick Bosa, Romello Height, Keion White, Mykel Williams, and Khalid Kareem lacks impact speed, bend and burst. Their PS options include Robert Beal, Villiami Fehoko and Ogbo Okoronkwo, but they may need more.

"It's a bad time of year to need additional edge rushers but (4) edge players I'd like to see them pursue: Kyle Kennard-Washington's PS. Azeez Ojulari-Las Vegas' PS. Nadame Tucker-Cleveland's PS. Michael Heldman-Kansas City's PS. All four have both explosive physical traits and good college production."

It's not the first time Krueger has pushed for edge-rush help. Last week, he floated free agents Leonard Floyd and Joey Bosa, who would have to come out of retirement, as possible options after the trade deadline.

To be fair, the effort was there on Sunday. The team totaled 26 pressures, 12 hurries, and 12 QB hits, according to Pro Football Focus.

The 49ers hit Prescott 10 times, and Bosa led the way with five pressures, four hurries, and one QB hit, according to PFF. Mykel Williams also had a sack wiped out by a penalty on cornerback Deommodore Lenoir.

But pressures don't show up on the scoreboard, and Dallas still put up 40 points.

The Giants took Ojulari No. 50 overall in 2021 out of Georgia, and he made an impact right away. He racked up eight sacks as a rookie, followed by 5.5 in just seven games in 2022 and six in 11 games in 2024.

In five seasons split between the Giants and Eagles, Ojulari has totaled 112 pressures, 67 hurries, 22 sacks, 19 QB hits, four forced fumbles, and two fumble recoveries.

However, staying on the field has always been the problem.

Ojulari signed a one-year deal with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025 but played just 67 snaps in three games, landing on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. His hometown Atlanta Falcons gave him a one-year, $1.4 million deal in March, then released him at final roster cuts. The Las Vegas Raiders signed him to their practice squad in early September.

Still, the 26-year-old has the burst Krueger is talking about. And he'd cost San Francisco nothing but a roster spot. Because Ojulari is on a practice squad, the 49ers could sign him straight to their 53-man roster without giving up a pick.

They might not be the only team kicking the tires either. With Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson injured, they could be in the market for Ojulari too

Given San Francisco's inability to actually finish sacks, Ojulari is a low-risk gamble worth taking.
